description: What a resource depends on, or what depends on it.

depth.description: forward: how many levels to follow, 1 being what the file loads itself. Default unlimited, which follows every class_name use too and in a project whose scripts name each other's classes reaches most of it: a game of a hundred scripts with large addons answered 488 files in about a megabyte from its main scene. A depth of 2 or 3 keeps the answer to what is near.

direction.description: forward: what this resource loads, with each reference closing a cycle marked circular and the cycle under circular_references, a script's dependencies including every script whose class_name it uses, marked by_class with the name, and the script of every autoload it names, marked by_autoload with the autoload's name. An ext_resource whose uid names another file than its path is followed to that file, as the engine loads it, with the path written under stale_path; one whose uid names no file the project has is followed by its path, as the engine does after warning, with the uid under unknown_uid; and a load or preload of a uid the project does not know is listed under that uid as missing. A shader's #include is followed as the preprocessor reads it, relative to the shader. A file the depth stops at carries beyond_depth, how many files it names that were not walked. A file's dependencies are listed at its first entry, and again further down only where the depth cut that list short and more is left; every other entry for a file naming any carries dependencies_listed_above. summary.total_resources is the file asked about, so 1; total_dependencies counts each file reached, directly or through another, once however many places load it; total_references counts the entries in the tree, and missing names every file referenced that does not exist, with the files referring to it. reverse: every file that refers to it and how, for a file that is gone as well while anything still refers to it, answered with exists: false (a missing file nothing refers to is refused, naming the nearest files), a scene instancing it, a script extending, preloading or loading it, and for a script with a class_name every use of that name, and for an autoload's script every use of the autoload's name, with autoload naming it. Each reference carries a kind: ext_resource, extends, preload, load, include or path for a reference by path, with stale_path when an ext_resource reaches it by its uid under another path, and unknown_uid when one names it by path beside a uid naming no file; setting, plugin, export_preset and import for one in project.godot, a plugin.cfg, export_presets.cfg or an import sidecar; class_name for a use of the declared name, the declaration itself being the script asked about; autoload for code naming the autoload. Three kinds are not uses: doc is a name inside a ## documentation comment, which renaming would break in the generated docs; comment is one in ordinary prose, which it would only make stale; and stale_path is an ext_resource naming it by a path the engine does not load, since its uid leads to the file under loads. summary.in_code is the count with those left out, which is the number to read when the question is whether anything still uses this. Default forward.

fileTypes.description: reverse: extensions to look in, plus "godot" for project.godot, "cfg" for plugin.cfg and export_presets.cfg, and "import" for import sidecars. Default all of tscn, tres, gd, gdshader, gdshaderinc, godot, cfg and import, since an autoload, the main scene and a plugin script are named only in the settings files.

includeBuiltin.description: forward: include the engine's own res://. resources. Default false.

projectPath.description: Absolute path to the project directory, the one holding project.godot.

resourcePath.description: File inside the project, such as "sprites/hero.png" or "materials/steel.tres".
